histories.MatterHistoryActionText: Upon motion duly seconded, the bill passed first reading and will be considered at the next regular meeting. The bill is referred to the Budget and Finance Committee and the Public Health and Safety Committee.

The bill was recommended for a three-meeting deferral by the Budget and Finance Committee and the Public Health and Safety Committee. Council Member Cortese moved to defer the bill to the September 1, 2026 Council meeting, which motion was seconded and approved by a voice vote of the Council.

The bill was recommended for deferral by the Budget and Finance Committee and recommended for a two-meeting deferral by the Public Health and Safety Committee. Council Member Cortese moved to suspend the rules of procedure to offer a two-meeting deferral. Without objection, Council Member Cortese moved to defer the bill to the October 6, 2026 Council meeting, which motion was seconded and approved by a voice vote of the Council.

The bill was approved by the Budget and Finance Committee and  the Public Health and Safety Committee. Council Member Cortese moved that the bill be deferred, which motion was seconded and approved by a voice vote of the Council.

Council Member Cortese moved that the bill be passed on second reading, which motion was properly seconded. Council Member Cortese offered a substitute bill and moved that it be adopted, which motion was seconded and approved by a voice vote of the Council.
Council Member Cortese moved that the bill be passed on second reading as substituted, which motion was seconded and approved by a voice vote of the Council.

matter.MatterTitle: An ordinance directing the Metropolitan Human Relations Commission to lead the development of a public awareness initiative to help improve prevention of young people’s engagement with violent online networks, including networks associated with nihilistic violent extremism and hate-based violent extremism; directing the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department and the Metropolitan Human Relations Commission to report their efforts to address these threats; and requesting that community partners serving young people and families assist in distributing educational materials developed through this initiative.

text:
..title
An ordinance directing the Metropolitan Human Relations Commission to lead the development of a public awareness initiative to help improve prevention of young people’s engagement with violent online networks, including networks associated with nihilistic violent extremism and hate-based violent extremism; directing the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department and the Metropolitan Human Relations Commission to report their efforts to address these threats; and requesting that community partners serving young people and families assist in distributing educational materials developed through this initiative.
..body
WHEREAS, violent online networks use online platforms and digital spaces to target young people and other vulnerable individuals for exploitation, coercion, radicalization, and other harmful conduct; and
WHEREAS, these networks may use grooming, manipulation, coercion, blackmail, and other tactics to gain the trust of young people, exploit their vulnerabilities, sexually exploit or abuse them, or encourage, pressure, or compel them to engage in self-harm, violence, animal abuse, or other harmful, dangerous, or unlawful conduct; and
WHEREAS, some of these networks and individuals are associated with nihilistic violent extremism, a term used by federal law enforcement to describe violence motivated by a desire to sow chaos, destruction, and social instability, while others may be motivated by different ideologies or criminal purposes; and
WHEREAS, hate-based violent extremist networks may similarly use online platforms and other means to recruit, radicalize, exploit, or encourage violence by young people and other vulnerable individuals; and
WHEREAS, incidents locally and nationally have highlighted the role that violent online networks and extremist content can play in influencing or encouraging acts of violence by young people, including school shootings; and
WHEREAS, the purpose of this ordinance is to help raise awareness and improve the prevention of the recruitment, radicalization, coercion, and exploitation of young people by violent online networks, including those associated with nihilistic violent extremism and hate-based violent extremism; and
WHEREAS, the Metropolitan Council denounces nihilistic violent extremism and desires to help young people, parents, caregivers, educators, and the broader community better understand these threats, recognize potential warning signs, and identify appropriate resources for prevention, intervention, and assistance; and 
WHEREAS, the Metropolitan Council expresses its support for the work underway by the Metropolitan Human Relations Commission to develop a public awareness initiative to help improve prevention of these threats to young people and families; and
WHEREAS, nihilistic violent extremism is a decentralized, largely online subculture where participants encourage violence with no coherent purpose, but as an expression of alienation, transgression, and meaning seeking; and 
WHEREAS, recent investigative reporting has shown cases where young people are drawn into these online communities. These children have become entangled with anonymous “handlers” who encourage destructive behavior, validate grievances, and frame violence as a pathway to fame or notoriety; and 
WHEREAS, these extremist tactics can include encouraging self-harm, exploiting vulnerable youth, and using coercion and blackmail to pressure individuals into escalating acts of violence, including suicide and school shootings; and 
WHEREAS, according to the U.S. Department of Justice, the perpetrator of the Antioch High School shooting in January 2025 claimed to have been motivated by “handlers” and extremist groups in carrying out the tragedy; and 
WHEREAS, the Metropolitan Council denounces nihilistic violent extremism and its tragic and corrosive effects and desires for the Metropolitan Government to take steps to prevent young people in Nashville and Davidson County from being exploited by these communities; and 
WHEREAS, it is in the best interest of the Metropolitan Government to coordinate a response that provides young people, families, caregivers, educators, youth-serving professionals, and the broader community with information and resources to recognize and respond to these threats; and, through the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department and the Office of the Mayor, to coordinate a response to educate parents and the broader community about the growing threat of nihilistic violent extremism targeting young people online; and 
WHEREAS, it is additionally crucial for these departments to work with Metropolitan Nashville Public Schools to ensure that parents and students are informed of this issue and a public awareness initiative to help improve prevention and better educate families, teachers, and the community about these threats and warning signs tied to this threat. 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ENACTED BY THE COUNCIL OF THE METROPOLITAN GOVERNMENT OF NASHVILLE AND DAVIDSON COUNTY: 
Section 1. This legislation is known and may be cited as the “Keep Kids Safe Online Act.”
Section 2. 1. That the Metropolitan Council hereby directs the Metropolitan Human Relations Commission (“MHRC”), in consultation with subject-matter experts, to lead the development of educational programming to better educate young people, families, caregivers, educators, youth-serving professionals, and the broader community about violent online networks, including those associated with nihilistic violent extremism and hate-based violent extremism; the methods used by these networks to groom, recruit, radicalize, manipulate, coerce, sexually exploit, or otherwise victimize young people; potential warning signs of victimization or engagement; and strategies to help prevent young people from being targeted or exploited by these networks. The educational programming should include information regarding circumstances in which a young person may be a victim of online exploitation, at risk of radicalization to violence, or being coerced or encouraged to engage in self-harm, violence, or other harmful conduct. 
The Metropolitan Nashville Police Department (“MNPD”) shall consult with MHRC to help shape the educational programming and provide their respective expertise, findings, and emerging information relevant to this initiative. All Metropolitan Government departments, agencies, offices, and commissions not specifically identified in this ordinance that possess relevant information, resources, or expertise concerning the online targeting, grooming, exploitation, or radicalization of young people shall cooperate with MHRC and provide relevant information and assistance in support of the development and ongoing implementation of the public awareness initiative, consistent with applicable law and confidentiality requirements.
Metropolitan Nashville Police Department and the Mayor’s Office, through the Office of Youth Safety, establish a coordinated framework to develop a training platform and/or public communication campaign to better educate families, teachers, and the community about the threats of nihilistic violent extremism and potential warning signs of possible engagement by children in Nashville and Davidson County. 
Section 3. That the Metropolitan Council directs that the public awareness initiative to help improve prevention shall be periodically reviewed and updated to reflect emerging violent online networks, recruitment and exploitation tactics, online platforms, terminology, and other developing threats to young people. The educational programming shall include a publicly accessible resource for young people, parents, caregivers, educators, students, youth-serving professionals, and other members of the community identifying potential warning signs, emerging tactics, prevention strategies, and appropriate resources for reporting concerns or seeking assistance.
Section 4. 2. That the Metropolitan Council further directs that MHRC and the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department submit a reports outlining its their efforts to address nihilistic violent extremism violent online networks, including those associated with nihilistic violent extremism and hate-based violent extremism, no later than one year following the effective date of this Ordinance. MHRC shall also provide to the Metropolitan Council a copy of the educational materials when they are completed or later updated.
Section 5. That the Metropolitan Council hereby goes on record as requesting that schools, youth-serving organizations, nonprofit organizations, and other community partners that serve or support young people and families work with MHRC and subject-matter experts to support the development and dissemination of the training, educational programming, information, and strategies developed through this initiative. The Metropolitan Council further requests that participating Metropolitan departments and agencies, including Metro Nashville Public Schools, the Metropolitan Council, the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department, MHRC, and the Juvenile Court of Nashville and Davidson County, along with community organizations and private institutions, use their platforms and appropriate communication channels to raise awareness and distribute the educational materials to young people, families, caregivers, educators, youth-serving professionals, and the broader community.
Section 3. That the Metropolitan Council hereby goes on record as requesting that Metropolitan Nashville Public Schools provides outward-facing educational efforts that inform parents of threats of nihilistic violent extremism and enables continued communications relative to this issue. 
Section 6. 4. This Ordinance shall take effect from and after its adoption, the welfare of Tthe Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County requiring it.

..Agenda Analysis
Analysis

This ordinance, as substituted, directs the Metropolitan Human Relations Commission (“MHRC”) in consultation with subject-matter experts, to lead the development of educational programming relative to identifying and countering the growing threat of violent online networks, including those associated with nihilistic violent extremism and hate-based violent extremism that targets and exploits young people in Nashville and Davidson County. 

The educational programming should include information regarding circumstances in which a young person may be a victim of online exploitation, at risk of radicalization to violence, or being coerced or encouraged to engage in self-harm, violence, or other harmful conduct. The Metropolitan Nashville Police Department (“MNPD”) would consult with MHRC to help shape the educational programming. All Metropolitan Government departments with relevant information, resources, or expertise shall also cooperate with MHRC and provide relevant information and support to this initiative.

The bill would require this public awareness initiative to be periodically reviewed and updated. The ordinance requires MNPD and MHRC to submit reports outlining its efforts to address nihilistic violent extremism no later than one year following the effective date of this ordinance.

The bill also requests that schools, youth-serving organizations, nonprofit organizations, participating Metropolitan departments, and other community partners that serve or support young people and families work with MHRC and subject-matter experts to support the development and dissemination of the initiative.
